key_insight: A hybrid pipeline that combines QAOA sampling with classical partitioning and repair can scale constrained quantum optimization to a 1,710-variable matching problem on thousand-node power-grid data.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical route to deploy current superconducting quantum hardware for large scheduling and energy-network optimization tasks that are too large for unpartitioned quantum encoding.
method: Spectrally partition the matching problem into hardware-manageable subproblems.
Run single-layer QAOA on each partition and repair infeasible samples classically with greedy fixes.
Use E-FCFW to assemble a sparse weighted decomposition from improved candidate matchings.
evidence_signal: On the PEGASE-1354 benchmark, repaired QAOA samples outperformed simulated annealing and random sampling, and spatial circuit packing cut hardware execution time by about 3×.
watch_item: Performance depends on partition size and quantum correlation retention, so overly small partitions or aggressive MPS truncation can degrade solution quality.
paper_title: Scaling Quantum Optimization to the Thousand-Qubit Scale with Distributed Quantum Sampling
